_comment: Arm 3: GL/GNN over the raw graph construction (#12). OS endpoint, 20-Study cohort, 5-fold Study-stratified CV (#7), stratified Efron Cox loss and lifelines CoxPHFitter decoder locked by #3, feature contract locked by #4. Architecture is encoder doc §6's recommended v1: type-aware Linear(width_t -> d) input embedding, L=2 relation-aware message passing with mean aggregation and a bare-identity residual, per-type LayerNorm, root readout z_G = h_v0^(L).
_construction: Rooted per-Subject subgraph: 5 node types (Subject, Diagnosis, Condition, Sample, PathologyDetail) and 5 forward relations (HAS_PRIMARY_DIAGNOSIS, HAS_SECONDARY_DIAGNOSIS, OF_CONDITION, PROVIDED_SAMPLE, HAS_PATHOLOGY) plus their 5 reverses. Not the 7/6 of #1: #4 §4-§5 removed Intervention and PhenotypeObservation, and #11 split HAS_DIAGNOSIS on isPrimaryDiagnosis.
_condition_flag: The Condition node keys on conditionId, amending #4 §2 (conditionName is corrupt on the live graph: 173 ids collapse to 54 names, and ICD10:C22.0 (liver) is labelled 'Malignant melanoma, NOS'). Keyed on identity it is the most severe cancer-type channel measured in this project -- R2_study = 0.948, against 0.793 for conditionSubtype, with 108 of 121 cohort conditionId values in exactly one Study. The within-Study Harrell C is immune to it by construction (#4 §6): a feature near-constant within a stratum cannot reorder within-Study pairs. The pooled secondaries (pooled_harrell_c, uno_c_ipcw) are exposed and must be read knowing Condition ~= Study.
_prior: message-passing.md §10.3 predicts a thin result: after Intervention left, the subgraph is one set (Samples, ~2 distinct types per Subject) plus a near-1:1 Diagnosis chain. A null result is pre-registered, not a failure. #13's trust gate decides whether any number here is believable.
